incident-bot: ALERT: high streaming tail latency detected on /v1/streaming (p99 > 10s) — incident_id=INC-2026-03-15-09. Pager: #oncall. Runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/streaming-tail
Jordan (oncall): ack — taking lead, starting triage. Paging SREs and runtime.
Maria (sre): looking — I can confirm a sharp p99 jump starting ~09:10 UTC. p95 ~1.2s -> 600ms after mitigation, p99 peaked ~12s. Error rate up ~2.3% (timeouts + aborted streams).
Maria (sre): quick metrics snapshot (PromQL):
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_stream_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
sum(rate(redwood_stream_errors_total[5m]))
```
Alex (runtime-eng): grabbing logs from streaming workers. Seeing backlog in prompt-constructor step (prompt_builder.parse_template). Tokenizer queue depth spiking, KV cache waits. Sample log: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] worker-7 prompt_builder: parse_template for request_id=abc123 took=1250ms schema=tool-schema-v2
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] worker-7 tokenizer: queue_depth=42 waiting_for_prefix_cache
[2026-03-15T09:11:03Z] worker-7 stream: stall detected, headroom=0
```
Alex (runtime-eng): hypothesis: expensive tool-schema expansion + JSON-mode validation per streaming chunk is blocking IO loop, increasing tail latency. Might be compounded by missing prefix cache hits for some templates.
Cassidy (product): any direct customer impact? We have a handful of enterprise flows relying on streaming for live UX. Are timeouts causing visible failures?
Maria (sre): short answer: yes for a small subset. We see ~1200 requests in the window with >5s latency; 18 requests returned stream timeouts (client side) — two belong to Dedicated customers with strict SLOs. Not a mass outage but severity → P1 for impacted customers.
Samir (infra): possible fast mitigations: 1) disable JSON-mode prevalidation on streaming path (cheap toggle), 2) route heavy streaming traffic to fallback model-compact, 3) increase streaming-worker pool temporarily. Which order preferred?
Jordan (oncall): I'll run (1) first — toggle JSON validation off for streaming, then watch for p99 improvement. If not enough, (2) and (3). Executing now.
Jordan (oncall): /runbook toggle-jsonmode --env=prod --path=/v1/streaming --value=false
deploy-bot: Route change request accepted. Change id=chg-8721. Applying to routing layer now.
Jordan (oncall): action applied. Also scaled streaming-workers from 8 -> 12 via k8s: `kubectl scale deploy/streaming-workers --replicas=12 -n inference-prod`
Maria (sre): within 90s of change: p95 back to ~700ms, p99 dropped to ~2.1s, error rate drop ~1.8%. Trend looks positive.
deploy-bot: Monitor alert cleared: streaming-tail-latency (p99) now under threshold. chg-8721 closed.
Alex (runtime-eng): good mitigation. Root cause likely: prompt constructor doing full JSON schema validate + heavy regex template expansion on hot path. Repro steps: run JSON-mode with large tool-schema -> parse_template takes >1s consistently.
Alex (runtime-eng): short-term follow-ups I'll open: 1) move JSON schema validation off hot path (async), 2) add prefix cache warmup for common templates, 3) optimize tokenizer queue backpressure handling. Creating ticket now.
Jordan (oncall): creating incident ticket and adding stakeholders. Summary: streaming p99 spike caused by prompt-constructor + JSON-mode prevalidation causing tokenizer queueing. Mitigation: disabled JSON-mode for streaming path + scaled workers. Customer impact: small number of Dedicated customers experienced timeouts; records logged and CSE notified.
Jordan (oncall): Handoff to @Li (oncall-next) in 30m. Li please monitor dashboards: p95/p99 for /v1/streaming, tokenizer_queue_depth, parse_template histograms.
Li (oncall-next): ack — will monitor for the next 2 hours and follow the postmortem actions. Please add runbook steps for toggling JSON-mode and ensuring traffic routing ids.
Cassidy (product): please loop in account reps for the two impacted Dedicated customers. I'll draft a brief statement and coordinate with support.
Samir (infra): post-incident immediate tasks: add temporary alert for parse_template > 300ms, add dashboard for JSON-mode toggles, ensure rollout gating for schema changes.
Maria (sre): adding timeline and metric captures to the incident ticket. Will attach flamegraphs and sample traces.
Jordan (oncall): closing active paging. Incident severity=P1 (customer impact, mitigated). Next: postmortem and follow-up tickets: RUNTIME-1942 (async schema), RUNTIME-1943 (template cache), SRE-1109 (alerts). :thumbsup:
Li (oncall-next): :eyes: I'll confirm stable in 30m and then move to monitoring-only.
incident-bot: NOTE: Please remember to fill the postmortem template: https://redwood/internal/incidents/postmortem-template. Deadline: 72 hours.
